testCases.name: test_case_2
testCases.input: What is positional encoding and why is it needed?
testCases.actualOutput:
According to Paper: Attention Is All You Need, positional encoding refers to the process of adding information about the relative or absolute position of tokens in a sequence to the input embeddings.

The authors state that "To evaluate if theTransformer can generalize to other tasks we performed experiments on English constituency parsing." This suggests that the Transformer model requires additional information to understand the order of tokens in a sequence, which is where positional encoding comes in.

In their work, they mention that there are many choices of positional encodings, learned and fixed. Specifically, they describe using sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: 

PE(pos,2i) sin(pos 100002i dmodel)
PE(pos,2i) cos(pos 100002i dmodel)

where pos is the position and i is the dimension.

The authors hypothesized that this sinusoidal function would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions. They also observe that replacing this sinusoidal positional encoding with learned positional embeddings has nearly identical results to the base model.

In summary, positional encoding is a way to provide additional information about the relative or absolute position of tokens in a sequence to help the Transformer model understand the order of tokens and make more accurate predictions.
testCases.expectedOutput: Positional encoding injects information about token positions using sine and cosine functions. It is needed because the Transformer has no recurrence or convolution so cannot inherently use sequence order.

testCases.name: test_case_4
testCases.input: How does scaled dot-product attention work?
testCases.actualOutput:
According to [Paper: Attention Is All You Need], Scaled Dot-Product Attention works by computing a weighted sum of the values, where the weight assigned to each value is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key.

In more detail, as described in section 3.2.1:

"3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention We call our particular attention mechanism Scaled Dot-Product Attention. The output is computed as a weighted sum of the values, where the weight assigned to each value is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key."

This means that for a given input query, set of keys, and values, scaled dot-product attention computes a weighted sum of the values, using the weights computed by taking the dot product of the query and keys (with a scaling factor of 1/dk) followed by applying the softmax function.

In practice, to prevent leftward information flow in the decoder, the authors mask out (set to zero) all values in the input of the softmax that correspond to illegal connections.
testCases.expectedOutput: Scaled dot-product attention computes dot products of queries with all keys, divides by square root of dk, applies softmax to get weights, then computes weighted sum of values.

1. Simple-language question answering and language modeling tasks.
2. English constituency parsing (both with large and limited training data).

Additionally, it was also compared to other models in translation tasks.
